scenes.heading: Diseases from dirty water
scenes.sub: Cholera · dysentery · typhoid · hepatitis A and E
scenes.narration: When floods come, the water we drink can make us sick. Floodwater carries sewage into wells, water tanks and food, and that spreads several serious diseases. The same simple steps protect your family from all of them.

scenes.heading: How they spread
steps: Floods carry them into water and food
scenes.narration: These diseases spread in the same way. The germs live in the faeces of sick people. When floodwater or overflowing latrines reach wells, tanks and food, the germs get in. Anyone who swallows them can fall ill, and can pass the germs on.

scenes.heading: Four diseases to know

cards.name: Hepatitis A and E
cards.sign: Yellow eyes and skin, dark urine

scenes.narration: Four of these diseases are worth knowing. Cholera causes sudden, watery diarrhoea, and can kill within hours. Dysentery is diarrhoea with blood. Typhoid fever brings a high fever that lasts for days, with headache and stomach pain. Hepatitis A and E attack the liver: the eyes and skin turn yellow, and the urine turns dark. Hepatitis E is especially dangerous for pregnant women.

scenes.heading: 1. Make water safe
steps: Bring it to a rolling boil
Let it cool with the lid on
scenes.narration: First, make drinking water safe. Bring the water to a rolling boil, with big bubbles, then let it cool with the lid on. If you cannot boil it, use water treatment tablets exactly as the packet says. Use safe water for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and making baby food.

scenes.heading: 2. Wash your hands with soap
times: Before eating or feeding a child
scenes.narration: Second, wash your hands with soap and clean water. Wet your hands and rub in soap. Scrub every part: palms, backs, between the fingers and under the nails. Rinse, and let them dry in the air. Do it after the toilet, after cleaning a child, before cooking, and before eating or feeding a child.

scenes.heading: 3. Keep faeces away from water
scenes.narration: Third, keep faeces away from water. Always use a latrine, never open ground, and keep latrines far from wells. Put children's faeces in the latrine too, and wash your hands afterwards.

scenes.heading: 4. Make food safe
steps: Cook it well, eat it hot
scenes.narration: Fourth, make food safe. Cook food well and eat it while it is hot. Wash fruit with safe water and peel it, and keep food covered.

scenes.heading: If someone falls ill
steps: Mix it exactly as the packet says
signs: A fever that will not go away
Pregnant, very weak, or cannot drink
scenes.narration: If someone gets diarrhoea, act fast. Start oral rehydration solution, O R S, straight away. Mix it with safe water exactly as the packet says, and give small sips often. Keep eating, and keep breastfeeding babies. Go to a health facility at once if there is blood in the diarrhoea, a fever that will not go away, or yellow eyes or skin, or if the person is pregnant, very weak, or cannot drink. Dysentery and typhoid need medicine from a health worker.

scenes.heading: Safe water. Clean hands. Quick ORS.
scenes.vaccine: Vaccines for cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A: take them where offered
scenes.narration: There are vaccines against cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A. Where health workers offer them, take them, and keep boiling water and washing hands. Safe water, clean hands, quick O R S. Share this with your family.
